readout_other: probabilistic reversal learning task (win-stay, learning rates); BOLD response to reward expectation and delivery
direction_notes: TUS to the NAcc increased reward sensitivity (win-stay, learning rate after reward) and BOLD response to reward expectation in NAcc relative to Sham and dACC TUS; dACC TUS did not change those measures.
safety_notes: 4-point symptom questionnaire on the day and the day after found no difference between TUS and Sham; reported symptoms were attributed to the MRI procedure. Simulated skull temperature rise mostly below 2 C and CEM43 below 0.1.

flags.reason: Four visits include one screening/MRI visit with no sonication; three visits had TUS-NAcc, TUS-dACC or Sham.
35 W/cm2 is the free-field Isppa kept constant; in situ values were simulated per participant but only appear in the supplement and Fig 1f.
Sham had the TPO turned off with the transducer placed to target the medial frontal cortex, plus bone-conducted sound mimicking the protocol; dACC TUS served as an active control site.
Authors report no difference between TUS and Sham; non-TUS symptoms (sleepiness, neck pain, headache, blurry vision) attributed to MRI.
Text gives 5 Hz PRF and a 200 ms pulse repetition interval.

provenance.notes: The paper also reports three DBS-NAcc patients (no ultrasound); not counted in n_subjects.
